notes: Heuristics for how consumer routers name and password their networks. These are starting points, not facts: they are labelled 'heuristic' wherever wifipilot shows them. Masks use hashcat syntax (?d digit, ?l lower, ?u upper, ?a all printable). Words are literal candidates.

tp-link.label: TP-Link
tp-link.note: TP-Link ships models that default to the SSID suffix digits and, on older firmware, an 8-digit numeric key.
tp-link.advice: The suffix in the ESSID (TP-Link_AB12) is often not the key; try the 8- and 10-digit numeric masks first.

netgear.label: NETGEAR
netgear.note: NETGEAR defaults to a dictionary word or a short random phrase; older WNR models use 'password'.
netgear.advice: Wordlist-first target: the factory key is often a common word, not a pattern.

fritz.label: AVM FRITZ!Box
fritz.note: FRITZ!Box factory keys are long decimal or hexadecimal strings printed on the case; the printed value is the ANonce-era default.
fritz.advice: A 16-digit mask is 10^16 — GPU-only, and only worth it with a known serial-number prefix.

telekom.label: Telekom / Speedport
telekom.note: Telekom routers often use the network name plus digits, or a numeric WLAN key.
telekom.advice: Derive the prefix from the ESSID exactly as printed (case matters in the candidate, not in the mask).

vodafone.label: Vodafone / Unitymedia
vodafone.note: Vodafone EasyBox keys are often 8-character mixed strings; Station keys are longer.
vodafone.advice: Small mask + big wordlist is usually the cheapest route here.

dlink.label: D-Link
dlink.note: D-Link routers vary: some are blank, some 8 digits, some 10 alphanumerics.
dlink.advice: Check whether the network is open first — a surprising number of D-Link defaults are.

asus.label: ASUS
asus.note: ASUS factory keys are often 10 digits or a short mixed string.
asus.advice: Try the vendor words before the mask; the masks are cheap to try anyway.

ubiquiti.label: Ubiquiti
ubiquiti.note: UniFi default keys are random 8-12 character strings; WPS is the usual way in, not cracking.
ubiquiti.advice: Random defaults are not crackable — look for WPS or a client-side weakness instead.

zte.label: ZTE
zte.note: ZTE ONT/router keys are frequently 8 digits or a short uppercase prefix plus digits.
zte.advice: Numeric masks are cheap; try them before any wordlist.

huawei.label: Huawei
huawei.note: Huawei uses 8 uppercase characters on some models, 8 digits on others.
huawei.advice: Two 8-character masks cover most of it; both are GPU-sized.

mikrotik.label: MikroTik
mikrotik.note: no factory PSK by default; the config is the target
mikrotik.advice: If it is still on defaults, the key is empty or 'admin' — try before cracking.

verizon.label: Verizon FiOS
verizon.note: 16-character mixed default printed on the router

orange.label: Orange Livebox
orange.note: first 8 characters of the WiFi key are the SSID suffix on some models
orange.advice: the SSID suffix is not the key, but it constrains it

linksys.label: Linksys
linksys.note: older models: 'admin' or blank; newer: random 8 characters

kpn.label: KPN
kpn.note: 10-digit numeric default on some Experia boxes
